name: Comic Pulp Mystery
description: Graphic-novel cel shading with heavy black outlines and one glowing focus at the centre of the frame — saturated teal and orange burning out of a rain-soaked night, lit by lightning, drawn with the energy of a pulp cover.
style_bible: Graphic-novel illustration in the register of a pulp paperback cover, drawn rather than photographed and printed rather than rendered. Line: every form is closed by a heavy black outline of confident, slightly uneven weight — thickest on the silhouette and on the shadow side, thinner inside the form, and thinnest on the details closest to the light — so the picture reads at card size as a set of black shapes before any colour is seen. Shading: flat cel shading only, two or at most three steps per surface with hard-edged boundaries between them, plus a single hard black shadow shape per object; no soft gradient, no airbrush, no blur, and no rendered specular. Colour: a night palette built from two saturated hues held against near-black — a cold teal that owns the wet street, the sky, the glass and every shadow, and a hot orange that owns light itself: the object's glow, the reflections it throws, the sodium of distant light, the bounce on a face. The two never mix into a muddy middle; where they meet they meet on a hard edge. Ground and unlit mass go to a dense blue-black, and the paper's own white is spent only on the very hottest core of the glow and on rain. Subject grammar: one thing in the frame is glowing and everything else is reacting to it — an object, a doorway, a screen, a light in water, a shape at the far end of a corridor. That glow is the only true light source and it is placed inside the frame, so figures and architecture are lit from a single low or central position with long hard-edged shadows thrown away from it. Weather and air: rain falls as long straight streaks of pale teal drawn at a consistent angle across the whole frame, breaking into small hard splash marks where it lands; standing water reflects the glow as a broken vertical smear; lightning breaks from behind the scene as one flat white-blue shape that silhouettes the skyline and leaves everything in front of it black. Texture: an even halftone or coarse dot screen laid over the flat colour, plus fine print grain and a faint misregistration on one channel, so the frame reads as something that came off a press. Framing: sixteen by nine, low or slightly tilted camera, strong diagonals, generous dark ground in one part of the frame so the composition has somewhere quiet, and a deliberate depth order of near silhouette, lit middle ground, black background. Mood: charged, wet, late, and one second before somebody understands what they are looking at. Keep the contract content-independent: no fixed individual, case, place, era, insignia or copied composition.
